A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CtrlHGen research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison despite the revised format and expanded experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on three knowledge graphs, component ablations, a controllability analysis and generated-hypothesis case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds LLM and augmentation-baseline comparisons, temperature sensitivity results, detailed reward analyses and a dialogue demonstration.

M1.justification: The core augmentation, conditional training, reward mixture and GRPO procedure remain unchanged. Appendix C.5 adds an inference extension: DeepSeek-V3 selects control conditions using user intent and previous-round hypotheses, conclusions and Jaccard scores before invoking CtrlHGen again.

E1.justification: The three knowledge graphs, thirteen logical patterns and five control types remain unchanged. Appendix C.5 adds a multi-round scenario requiring adaptation to evolving user intentions, demonstrated through a four-turn song example; it adds no benchmark dataset or user study.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with GPT-4o, Kimi K2, Grok-3, DeepSeek-V3, GPT5(Thinking) and DeepSeek-V3+RAG in Tables 2 and 4. Tables 8–9 additionally compare Logic-Gen and AbductiveKGR+condition token against CtrlHGen after supervised training. The retained unconditional rows are explicitly attributed to AbductiveKGR.

E3.justification: New protocols include LLM prompting with two-hop graph triples, specified reasoning modes and temperatures, a GPT5 temperature sweep, and supervised-only augmentation comparisons under two DBpedia50 controls. These substantially broaden the evaluation design. The original splits, observation cap, metrics and documented training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds temperature sensitivity testing, per-pattern analysis of the condition-adherence reward, LLM error examples and a multi-round dialogue case. These examine exploration versus adherence, pattern-dependent reward effects and structural reasoning failures beyond the retained component ablations and relation-count visualization.

E5.justification: Both versions report means with standard deviations, and v2 extends that convention to new comparisons. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are disclosed.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original reward-ablation values remain identical, with the latter moved from Table 2 to Table 3. v2 adds extensive comparator and diagnostic results. For example, its supervised DBpedia50 pattern comparison reports Jaccard scores of 70.1 for CtrlHGen, 69.5 for Logic-Gen and 68.2 for AbductiveKGR+condition token. Figure 9 also corrects v1 Figure 8's erroneous music-genre conclusions to organization entities.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 and Equations 1–8 retain the same mathematical content, with no added theorems or proofs. The quantifier wording correction and expanded Smatch explanation clarify existing material without changing its formal substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing controllable KG abduction, addressing complex hypotheses through decomposition and reward design, and improving semantic quality and adherence on three datasets. Adding 'reward' to oversensitivity clarifies the existing challenge.

C2.justification: v2 expands interpretations of LLM structural errors, conflicts with graph knowledge, RAG's limited structural benefits and pattern-dependent reward tradeoffs. It also discusses interactive applicability. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit limitations concerning per-graph retraining costs and the absence of composite-condition experiments.

D1.justification: v2 specifies twelve decoder layers, explains the AMR conversion used for Smatch, and supplies LLM-generation and condition-selection prompts. It removes v1's explanation of ID-only encoding and semantic-leakage prevention. Existing hyperparameters, hardware and code-access information remain unchanged; the added layer detail does not establish an architecture change.

R1.justification: The related-work survey and core novelty positioning remain largely intact. v2 adds citations supporting Logic-Gen, Smatch, Transformer architecture and contemporary LLM comparisons, and extends its positioning against prompted and retrieval-augmented LLM reasoning.

P1.justification: Much of the original prose and main section order is preserved. v2 makes localized introduction and results rewrites, expands the Smatch explanation, moves detailed case discussion into Section 4.5, reorganizes Appendix C, and updates author information, citation style and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2 and 4–9 and Figures 7, 10 and 11, while relocating the original reward table and case figures. Several introductory diagrams are redrawn, and Figure 5's axes now begin at zero instead of 0.4. The conference template also changes headers, author layout and figure placement.

improvement.justification: The supervised comparator experiments in Tables 8–9, targeted analyses, disclosed prompts and corrected entity-case conclusions improve support for the unchanged method. These gains are tempered by removed transfer and composite-control limitations and new reporting inconsistencies: GPT5's Table 2 Smatch is 32.9, whereas its Table 4 entries average 48.5. Overall, comparative support improves, but the reporting weaknesses limit the gain.
